presets.summary: 0.25 Hz binaural beats during a daytime nap shortened latency to N2 and N3 slow-wave sleep in healthy young adults.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Very-low-frequency beat is intended to promote very slow cortical oscillations associated with initiating slow-wave sleep, reducing sleep latency; EEG entrainment at this frequency is subtle.

citations.title: Binaural beats at 0.25 Hz shorten the latency to slow-wave sleep during daytime naps

presets.summary: 3 Hz binaural beats during nocturnal sleep increased N3 (deep) sleep duration and altered sleep-stage distribution in a pilot study.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Beat at 3 Hz targets delta activity linked to N3 slow-wave sleep, potentially stabilizing deep sleep and influencing stage transitions.

citations.title: A Novel Insight of Effects of a 3-Hz Binaural Beat on Sleep Stages During Sleep

presets.summary: Dynamic 0–3 Hz binaural beats embedded in music improved subjective sleep quality and autonomic markers compared with control audio.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Slowly varying low-frequency differences aim to nudge networks toward slow oscillations and delta activity while shifting autonomic balance toward parasympathetic dominance.

citations.title: Effect of Dynamic Binaural Beats on Sleep Quality: A Proof-of-Concept Study with Questionnaire and Biosignals

presets.summary: Low-frequency binaural beat programs (around 2–7 Hz) improved global sleep quality and insomnia severity in adults with insomnia.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Repeated exposure to low-frequency beats fosters slower EEG activity during sleep onset and may reduce hyperarousal contributing to insomnia.

presets.summary: A single 20-minute session of 4–7 Hz auditory beat stimulation, including 6 Hz, reduced somatic and cognitive state anxiety in adults taking anxiolytics.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Theta-range beats combined with calming audio may enhance relaxation, modulate limbic networks, and reduce anxiety-related autonomic arousal.

Effects of binaural beat therapy with different frequencies on anxiety and depression among college students

presets.summary: College students exposed for 20 minutes to 6, 10, or 25 Hz binaural beats embedded in natural sounds showed reduced anxiety and improved heart-rate-variability markers.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Multiple beat frequencies in theta, alpha, and beta ranges appear to reduce state anxiety partly via autonomic nervous system modulation; no clear winner among specific frequencies.

citations.title: Effects of binaural beat therapy with different frequencies on anxiety and depression among college students

presets.summary: Preoperative 10 Hz binaural beat stimulation has been used in several trials to reduce state anxiety and sometimes anesthetic requirements in surgical patients.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Alpha entrainment is linked to relaxed wakefulness and may lower preoperative anxiety by shifting cortical rhythms and supporting parasympathetic dominance.

Binaural beat stimulation as a tool to reduce preoperative anxiety in patients undergoing elective surgery and general anesthesia

presets.summary: Low-frequency binaural beats (≤7 Hz) embedded in music reduced anxiety and improved tolerance in multiple invasive procedures such as bronchoscopy and colonoscopy.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Slow beats during procedures help distract, reduce anticipatory anxiety, and support autonomic stability, with modest or variable effects on pain ratings.

presets.summary: Daily 30-minute sessions of familiar music embedded with 10 Hz alpha binaural beats over several weeks reduced depression scores in older adults.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Alpha entrainment plus emotionally meaningful music may reduce hyperarousal and negative affect via relaxation and limbic–autonomic interactions.

presets.summary: Music containing 10 Hz binaural beats decreased heart rate and systolic blood pressure and improved HRV indices in older adults during a single listening session.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Promoting alpha rhythms is associated with relaxed but awake states and supports parasympathetic activation, lowering physiological stress markers.

presets.summary: Twice-weekly 20-minute 6 Hz binaural beat sessions over several weeks reduced perceived pain severity in clinical samples.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Theta beats likely affect cognitive–affective aspects of pain, shifting attention and emotional appraisal rather than nociceptive transmission.

presets.summary: Short daily 10-minute exposure to 6 Hz binaural beats for one month enhanced ERP markers (N200/P300) and aspects of attention and working memory.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: 6 Hz stimulation entrains theta activity and may strengthen frontoparietal networks involved in attention and cognitive control.

presets.summary: 10 Hz binaural beats consistently increase alpha-band power and are widely used for relaxed yet alert states in non-clinical users.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Alpha entrainment reduces excessive beta activity and supports a calm, focused state often associated with meditative awareness.

presets.summary: 16 Hz binaural beats reliably increased EEG power at the beat frequency in controlled experiments, confirming robust beta-band entrainment.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Direct enhancement of 16 Hz beta oscillations may support vigilance and task engagement, although downstream cognitive benefits remain inconsistent.

presets.summary: 20–30 minutes of 40 Hz binaural beats enhanced gamma-band activity, improved working-memory performance, and showed mood benefits in small samples.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: 40 Hz beats entrain gamma oscillations involved in information binding and working memory, potentially supporting cognition and affect regulation.

presets.summary: Low-beta (12–15 Hz) beats are commonly used in neurofeedback for attention; binaural beats around 15 Hz are explored for focus, but controlled ADHD data are limited.
presets.therapeutic_mechanism: Enhancing SMR/low-beta activity may counter excess theta and support sustained attention; evidence is mostly extrapolated from neurofeedback rather than direct binaural trials.

notes.carrier_frequency_flexibility: Most papers emphasize the beat (difference) frequency; carriers between roughly 100 and 500 Hz are commonly used and can be tuned for comfort as long as the interaural difference matches the target beat.[web:22][web:34]
notes.evidence_quality: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses highlight that while EEG entrainment at alpha, beta, and gamma frequencies is replicable, clinical outcomes (sleep, mood, pain, cognition) are small to moderate and not uniformly reproducible; presets should be treated as experimental tools, not proven therapies.[web:25][web:36][web:61]
notes.safety_considerations: Use moderate levels (<70 dB), avoid for people with photosensitive or sound-triggered epilepsy without medical clearance, and do not use during driving or operating machinery.[web:66]
